title: Qualitative & Quantitative Assessment of Human Islets Using Dithizone (DTZ)
author: Integrated Islet Distribution Program
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bk5vky66
materials: Assemble all items described in the Materials section.

steps.title: Prepare DTZ Stain
steps.instruction: Prepare the Dithizone (DTZ) staining solution while observing all safety precautions for DMSO.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 50 mg dithizone in 10 mL DMSO.
Add DPBS to bring the total volume to 50 mL.
Filter the combined solution using a 0.45 μm nylon filter.
Place the solution in a 50 mL conical tube and label as 'Dithizone Stain or DTZ' with the preparation date/time, expiration date/time (24 hours after preparation), and initials of the preparer.

steps.title: Sample the Islet Suspension
steps.instruction: Collect representative samples of the islet suspension for quantitation and purity assessment.

substeps.instruction: Mix the final islets suspension gently but thoroughly by inverting the islet prep in a conical tube 2-3 times (do not swirl).
Using a widebore tip pipettor, take replicate 100-200 µL sample volumes from the 100 mL final prep, ensuring the sample is taken from the middle of the suspension.
Perform two duplicate counts using two separate technicians or two separate counts by one technician.

steps.title: Stain and Prepare for Counting
steps.instruction: Stain the islet samples and prepare the counting dish.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 drops (30 μL) of the DTZ solution to the islets sample.
Allow staining for 1–2 minutes at room temperature.
Cover the bottom of the counting dish with DPBS to approximately ½ the height of the dish.

steps.title: Count Actual Islets (AI)
steps.instruction: Examine the sample under a microscope to identify and tally red-stained islets.

substeps.instruction: Use a 10x eyepiece and 4x objective for a total magnification of 40x.
Methodically scroll through the dish from side to side and top to bottom using the grid lines as a guide.
Count islets within the perimeter of the grid's squares, including only islets touching the top and right lines (exclude bottom and left lines).
Tally the number of Actual Islets (AI) in each diameter group using a manual or electronic cell counter, based on a calibrated reticle.
Do not count islets smaller than 50 μm.

steps.title: Calculate IEQ and Islet Index
steps.instruction: Determine the Total Islet Equivalents (IEQ) and the Islet Index (II) using the collected data.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the dilution factor: Dilution Factor = [(mL total volume / µL sample volume) X 1000]. (Example: 100 µL sample from 100 mL total = 1000 dilution factor).
Input the tally data into the Excel Spreadsheet (Attachment 1) to calculate Total Actual Islets (∑ AI) and Total Islet Equivalents (∑ IEQ).
Convert AI in each range to IEQ using the conversion factor (normalizing AI to 150 μm sized islet).
Multiply both the total AI and IEQ by the dilution factor for the Final AI count and Final IEQ Count.
Calculate the Islet Index (II) by dividing the IEQ by the AI (calculated automatically in Attachment 1).

steps.title: Assess Quality and Purity
steps.instruction: Grade the islet quality and estimate the percentage of purity.

substeps.instruction: Determine the Islet Quality Grade using the provided chart and Islet Ranking Guide (Attachment 2).
Estimate the percent purity to the nearest 5% by comparing the portion of red-stained islets to all tissue (islets, acinar, and ductal cells).
Record results on Attachment 1.

steps.title: Capture and Upload Digital Images
steps.instruction: Document the islet preparation with digital photography.

substeps.instruction: Gently swirl the count sample to center the islets in the dish.
Take a well-focused digital photo at 10x-40x magnification following the center's SOP.
Label and save the image with RRID#, date, time (prior to broadcast), and magnification.
Upload images to the IIDP website and match background grid lines per online instructions.

steps.title: Perform Repeat Evaluations
steps.instruction: Re-evaluate the islets if necessary before distribution.

substeps.instruction: Repeat all counting, grading, purity, and viability estimates and digital image uploads if more than 6 hours have passed since the original broadcast evaluations prior to packaging.
Update broadcast records under the 'Confirm Islet Information' section and repeat procedures for every subsequent 24-hour rebroadcast/shipment.
